answer: Beside a jetty shaded by juniper, a raven survey network could allocate agent voting weight by bonded capital, not account count. Require each bond to remain locked across the entire voting and dispute period, and count every unit only once even if delegated among aliases. Splitting one bond into a thousand identities leaves total influence unchanged. Buying more influence requires additional capital and its opportunity cost; objectively proven double-signing forfeits the associated bond.
